newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt pound interbank rates fall in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Egypt pound interbank rates fall in liquid market.

text.p: Overnight and one-week interbank rates on the Egyptian pound fell on Monday, with few bankers dealing in a liquid private-sector market.
One banker said he dealt at 8-7/8 to nine percent, and four others said they did not perform any overnight deals but heard rates were slightly higher at between nine and 9-1/4 percent.
Overnight rates were between 9-3/8 and 9-3/4 on Sunday.
"The market is very liquid and I have a lot of money. No one is taking and no one is offering," said one banker.
Bankers again on Monday cited the central bank's acceptance of few bids in its 91-day treasury bill auction last week as one factor behind the unusually high liquidity.
The bank had asked for 700 million pounds and accepted bids for 761.75 million, rejecting bids for 881.75 million.

One-week rates on Monday were put at 9-1/8 by the only banker of the five who had a deal. Another said he was inactive but heard one-week rates were higher at 9-1/2 percent. One week rates were between 9-1/2 and 10-1/8 percent on Sunday.
Public-sector banks kept their rates steady at 10-1/2 percent on Sunday.
